actor: Technical steering chair, Open Secure AI Alliance working groups
job: Chartering the alliance's working groups on identity, permissions, isolation, guardrails, logs, model formats, multi-model scanning and secure coding workflows.
outcome: Published specifications whose normative requirements land on the harness the deployer runs, with no clause addressed to a hosted closed-weight model API.
motivation: Thirty-seven partners can ship a scope covering artifacts they already hold; anything reaching OpenAI, Google or Anthropic's endpoints needs those vendors' cooperation.

task.who: Alliance technical steering committee and working-group chairs
task.what: Charter working groups around deployer-held artifacts
task.where: Open Secure AI Alliance technical charter and scope documents
task.why: Only artifacts members hold can be specified without vendor consent
task.how: Linux Foundation Akrites and OpenSSF working-group process

actor: Project governance manager, Linux Foundation Akrites initiative
job: Onboarding the six formation contributions from NVIDIA, Hugging Face, HPE, IBM, Red Hat, Microsoft and SpaceXAI into neutral foundation governance.
outcome: Six deployer-run projects hosted under foundation governance: a weights format, workload identity, signed patches, an agent-harness framework, a scanning harness and a coding agent.
motivation: Each contribution can be donated unilaterally because it acts on the deployer's side; a hosted API cannot be donated by anyone but its operator.

task.who: Akrites initiative and OpenSSF project intake staff
task.what: Onboard the six formation contributions into foundation governance
task.where: Linux Foundation Akrites and OpenSSF project intake review
task.why: Deployer-side code can be donated without the serving vendor
task.how: Contributor licence agreements and technical charter review

actor: Conformance programme lead, Open Secure AI Alliance
job: Defining what an alliance conformance profile tests and which evidence a certifying deployer must produce from its own environment.
outcome: A certification whose every criterion is verifiable from deployer-side logs, workload identities and signed artifacts, requiring nothing from the serving vendor.
motivation: A criterion demanding attested inference records from OpenAI, Google or Anthropic is untestable while none of the three publishes such an attestation.

task.what: Scope conformance criteria to deployer-producible evidence
task.where: Alliance conformance profile drafts and certification test suites
task.why: Vendor-attested criteria are untestable with no vendor attestation shipping
task.how: Self-run test suites over SPIFFE, SPIRE and Safetensors artifacts

actor: Open-source release engineer, model-lab alliance contributor
job: Preparing SpaceXAI's Grok Build terminal coding agent for release and staging the stated plan to publish the Grok line's weights.
outcome: Lab contributions that are entirely artifacts a user holds and runs — a terminal client and a weights file — never the hosted service.
motivation: Releasing client code and weights buys standing in the alliance at no cost to the hosted inference product SpaceXAI still sells.

task.who: Model-lab open-source and developer-tools engineering team
task.what: Release the terminal coding agent and publish weights
task.where: Public source repository and open-weight distribution channels
task.why: Deployer-side giveaways cost the hosted inference product nothing
task.how: Open-source licensing and public repository release

actor: Platform security engineer, open model hosting platform
job: Extending Safetensors signing and scanning coverage over the weights, shards and repositories Hugging Face hosts after the intrusion it contained.
outcome: A hardened artifact surface — hashable, signable, scannable files such as Kimi K3's 96 safetensors shards — that alliance specifications can address.
motivation: Hugging Face was breached and could only reconstruct more than 17,000 recorded actions by running open-weight GLM 5.2 on its own hardware.

task.who: Platform security and model-artifact integrity team
task.what: Extend signing and scanning across hosted weight artifacts
task.where: Hugging Face model repositories and Safetensors tooling
task.why: Only artifacts somebody holds can be hashed and pinned
task.how: Safetensors format validation and signed repository provenance checks

actor: Enterprise security architect, alliance member deploying agents
job: Submitting agent-deployment requirements to the alliance's working groups covering workload identity, permission scoping, isolation and log retention inside their own estates.
outcome: Specifications written to controls these buyers can implement themselves, because Capital One, DoorDash and Cisco control the harness but not the model endpoint.
motivation: A requirement they can satisfy in their own environment ships now; one needing OpenAI, Google or Anthropic to change product waits indefinitely.

task.who: Enterprise AI platform security and governance teams
task.what: Submit deployment control requirements to alliance working groups
task.where: Alliance working-group requirement intake and member review cycles
task.why: Controls inside their own estate ship without vendor change
task.how: SPIFFE and SPIRE workload identity plus agent log retention

actor: Industry-affairs lead, hosted frontier lab (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic)
job: Deciding whether to put the lab's name on the Open Secure AI Alliance partner roster without committing code or conformance obligations.
outcome: At least one of OpenAI, Google or Anthropic appearing on the alliance's published partner roster, contributing nothing to its technical output.
motivation: NVIDIA's July 24 open-weights letter went from twenty-five signatories to roughly fifty within a day, with OpenAI and Google among the additions.

task.what: Approve alliance roster membership without contribution commitments
task.where: Alliance membership agreement and published partner roster
task.why: A logo answers the alliance's founding argument at low cost
task.how: Standard consortium membership agreement with no contribution clause

actor: Government-affairs lead, hosted frontier lab policy team
job: Working the White House voluntary frontier-model framework, due to be finalized August 1, 2026, and its pre-release agency review of up to thirty days.
outcome: Provider-side disclosure handled as a voluntary government review for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, never as a procurement clause an alliance profile could cite.
motivation: A federal contract clause requiring inference records would give the alliance something to point at, and a provider-side annex would follow quickly.

task.what: Keep provider attestation duties voluntary in the federal framework
task.where: White House frontier-model framework consultations and agency reviews
task.why: A procurement clause would seed an alliance provider-side annex
task.how: Comment submissions and up-to-thirty-day pre-release review commitments
